pages/account/strings.en.json.faq.lockProtects.a: The passcode lock is part of the Hub on the web; the Hub in a terminal has none. On the web, once locked, people who pick up your device see only the lock screen. It locks after the time you pick, and when you leave the app if you turn that on; inside a Board program it can wait up to 15 minutes longer. Each tab and window locks and unlocks on its own; Lock now locks them all. It doesn't encrypt your sign-in: someone who can read what the web Hub stores on the device (developer tools, malware, a rooted phone) can still use it. The phone may show a preview of the Hub in its app switcher. Your account on other devices is not affected.
pages/account/strings.en.json.faq.lockScope.q: Where does the passcode apply, and what removes it?
pages/account/strings.en.json.faq.lockScope.a: The lock belongs to the Hub on the web, in the one place you set it; the Hub in a terminal has none. There, each tab and window locks on its own, and opening the Hub again asks for the passcode. Signing out keeps the passcode there; to remove it, use Remove passcode, or the Forget action on its lock screen. After you sign in again, the Hub still asks for it. Clearing the site's data removes the lock and signs you out of the Hub there. Notices already shown on that device stay there.
pages/account/strings.en.json.pw.unsureTitle: Leave the Hub and sign in again
pages/account/strings.en.json.check.unknownPw: We cannot tell from here whether the password was changed. It may have been. Leave the Hub, then sign in again with the new password; if that fails, the old one still works.
pages/account/strings.en.json.check.checkLinePw: Check again: reads your account again, but it can't show whether the password changed. Signing in after you leave the Hub shows which password works.
pages/account/strings.en.json.faq.checkAgain.a: When the Hub can't tell whether a change went through, it keeps a note instead of calling it done or failed. Check again reads your account again to see whether the change is there; if it still can't tell, the note stays. Stop tracking makes the Hub stop following the change. It doesn't undo the change or mark it as failed, and doing the change again may apply it twice. For a password change, signing in after you leave the Hub shows which password works.

pages/vault/strings.en.json.faq.scope.a: Global entries are shared by every realm and by tools that run without one. The entries of a realm belong to that realm. The same name in another realm, or in Global, is a different entry. Pick a realm from the realm menu at the top (Alt+R) to see its own entries.
pages/vault/strings.en.json.faq.showValue.a: Open the entry and press Show value to show it, or Copy to copy it without showing it. The value is read only then. Hiding it or closing the entry removes it from this page; the next press reads it again. An encrypted value asks for its password first; the password never leaves this device. JSON values are shown formatted, with Raw for the exact text; Copy always copies the exact stored value. You can also show the encrypted form, to paste where a tool expects it.
pages/vault/strings.en.json.faq.encrypt.a: The value is encrypted on this device before it is sent, and tools need the password to read it. To open an encrypted value here, enter its password; the password never leaves this device. An entry shown as "Not marked" has no encryption recorded. To protect its value, use Replace value and tick Encrypt with a password. The Hoody SDK, CLI and agent use the same encrypted form, so they can read it with the password.
pages/vault/strings.en.json.value.desc: Read only on Show value or Copy; hiding it removes it from this page.
pages/vault/strings.en.json.value.stale: The view changed while it was being read. Press Show value again.
pages/vault/strings.en.json.edit.valueDesc: Hidden as you type. Use Show what you typed to check it.
pages/vault/strings.en.json.faq.valueInput.a: A name uses letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore, up to 100 characters. Names starting with "hoody." belong to Hoody's own tools. A value is hidden as you type; use Show what you typed to check it. Line breaks are kept, so you can paste a whole key or certificate. It is saved exactly as typed, unless you encrypt it. Replacing a value overwrites the old one, and the old value is not shown here.
pages/vault/strings.en.json.faq.vaultFor.a: Values your tools and agents read by name: tokens, passwords, settings. Add a value your tools or agents should read by name; you can encrypt it with a password first. The list does not show values. In an entry, the value is read only when you press Show value or Copy, and is removed from the page when you hide it or close the entry.

pages/vault/strings.en.json.value.why.a: The value is read only when you press Show value or Copy; hiding it or closing the entry clears it. An encrypted value's password stays on this device.

pages/guide/strings.en.json.look.body: Light or dark follows your terminal's background, read once when the Hub starts. If the terminal does not report it in time and COLORFGBG does not name it, the Hub uses dark.
pages/guide/strings.en.json.build.find: These steps are for the web Hub, since a terminal has no developer tools. To find the call behind something the Hub shows, do it in the web Hub with the Network tab open, then give your agent the method and address.
pages/guide/strings.en.json.recipe.3.body: Name a realm, then pick it from the realm menu at the top (Alt+R). Everything here follows it.
pages/guide/strings.en.json.realms.lede: One realm per client, project or experiment. Pick a realm from the realm menu at the top (Alt+R) and every list and new thing follows it. Keys can be limited to one realm, so an agent you connect for a client sees only that client.

pages/realms/strings.en.json.faq.switchRemove.a: Pick a realm, or All realms, from the realm menu at the top (Alt+R). An empty realm may not reopen after the Hub starts again; pick it again from the menu. There is no Delete realm: a realm is listed while something is in it or it has a name. To remove one, take its computers, projects, servers and keys out of it, then clear its name with Rename realms… in the realm menu.

pages/notifications/strings.en.json.faq.bellInbox.q: How do the count and the Inbox work?
pages/notifications/strings.en.json.faq.bellInbox.a: The number beside Notifications in the sidebar counts your unread notices. The Hub checks for new ones from time to time while it is open and in front. Every notice stays in the Inbox until you mark it read. Read notices move to the Archive.
pages/notifications/strings.en.json.faq.timing.a: New notices may take a while to appear. The Hub checks from time to time while it is open and in front.
pages/notifications/strings.en.json.faq.browser.a: These alerts are part of the Hub on the web; the Hub in a terminal shows none. There, an alert is a pop-up about a new notice. It works only while the web Hub is open in a tab you are not looking at, in the place where you turned it on. An alert shows a short title and a fixed line to open the Hub, never the notice's message. Alerts are optional and are turned on in the web Hub, separately in each place you use it: turning them on in one does nothing for the others. You may be asked for permission when you turn them on. Other Hub activity, such as a Bot waiting for you, can use the same alerts.

pages/computers/strings.en.json.faq.snapshotsAndBackups.a: A snapshot saves the whole computer as it is now, kept by Hoody, and you can start a new computer from any of them. A zip backup downloads chosen folders of the computer to your device as .zip files, one per folder; the download goes straight from the computer and runs outside the Hub. Restoring a snapshot puts the computer back to how it was when the snapshot was taken, and files and settings changed since then are lost.
pages/computers/strings.en.json.current.ask.body: The top bar then shows {{name}}. Pages that work on one computer at a time work on it. Nothing on {{name}} changes. This Hub keeps the choice until you quit it.

pages/billing/strings.en.json.faq.retrySafe.a: When the Hub can't confirm a purchase, payment or upgrade, it asks you to check first (Servers for a purchase). Send the same request again repeats that request, so it is never charged twice. A rental is different: Check again on an unconfirmed rental only reads it back, and renting again anyway can give you two servers and two charges. Start a new purchase on an unconfirmed reservation can charge twice too. The Hub asks you to confirm both first. If this device can't save a new request, it is not sent; if it can't stop two Hubs paying twice, the Hub asks you to pay on the web.
